why_a_structured_supersedes_field: C5 and C6 recorded what they replaced in free prose, which no checker could resolve, so a stale canary could not be retired except by a human noticing. 'supersedes_canary' is the machine-readable form check_canary_freshness.py reads; a canary nothing supersedes must still describe the working tree.
supersedes_reason: check_canary_freshness.py, added in this same decision, reports both stale against current bytes: C5 pins stop_hook_sha256 dc19da4d against 0533da88, and C6 pins start_hook_sha256 af8f7016 against 8b283512. Neither was edited to hide that -- retained attestations are evidence and are not rewritten to satisfy a checker. They are retired by replacement, which is what a superseding canary is for.
method: SubagentStart dispatched with ACTIVE_RUN naming the canary run, so a real Start-time lease exists. ACTIVE_RUN then repointed to the DECOY run. ACTIVE_RUN read, SubagentStop dispatched, ACTIVE_RUN read again -- one shell command, no intervening work -- so the consume instant is bracketed rather than merely preceded.
first_attempt_blocked: The first dispatch was BLOCKED, correctly: no Start-time lease existed and the hook refused to fall back to the mutable ACTIVE_RUN pointer. That refusal is the property this canary exists to demonstrate, so it is recorded rather than discarded. The retry was written to stop_event_c7_attempt2.json, never over attempt 1, under the retry-safe naming rule established at D-070 Part B7.
resolution_limit: consumed_at is written with timespec='seconds', so sub-second ordering is unprovable and is NOT claimed. What is established is the pointer state across the dispatch, which is what obligation 4 asks.
what_this_does_not_claim: This canary shows the pointer did not decide the consume. It does not address the stated residual that harness and subagents share one OS user, so a deliberately misbehaving agent can still forge repo-local artifacts.
